newsitem.title: UK: IBCA says affirms P&O ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA says affirms P&O ratings.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, said on Thursday it affirmed the long-term A minus and short-term A2 ratings of The Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Company (P&O).

"The rating action follows today's announcement that P&O has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Stena Line AB to merge both companies' ferry interests on the short sea routes on the English Channel," IBCA said in a statement.
It said the new joint venture company, P&O Stena Line, will be 60 percent owned by P&O and 40 percent owned by Stena Line, though both companies will have equal voting rights.
"The new company will have gross assets of 410 million stg, financed by approximately 100 million stg of equity and 310 million stg of debt," it said.

"The move is an attempt to improve profitability of the ferry operations and to provide stiffer competition for Eurotunnel, which has quickly become the market leader as a result of aggressive price discounting since opening in 1994," IBCA said.

"It had been widely anticipated following the UK government's decision in July to lift a ban preventing P&O from discussing cooperation with rivals. The formal agreement is expected to be signed in November 1996 but will remain subject to the receipt of the necessary regulatory approval."
IBCA said the transaction followed the announcement last month of P&O's decision to merge its container business in a 50:50 joint venture with the Dutch firm Nedlloyd.
"P&O announced in early 1996 its intention to raise up to one billion stg through asset disposals and the deals with Royal Nedlloyd and Stena Line form part of this strategy," IBCA said.

"P&O needs to generate funds to improve its financial profile and finance the significant capital investment requirements of its core businesses as it attempts to meet its targeted 15 percent return on capital employed."
